terra.problem: The psalm does not say the watchmen stay up all night.
“He gives a gift” follows Solomon as its subject, but the verse says the LORD gives sleep.
The explanation places the sleep after the early rising and late toiling and calls it a night's sleep. The verse gives neither detail.
Saying one would expect Solomon to take credit for children puts him down without a basis in the text.
“Mine included” gives Papa Dorin knees, inconsistent with his stamper body and gold base.
The ending merely repeats that the song names two things. It is generic filler rather than Papa Dorin's voice.
It says the olive shoots are gathered at the table. The song compares the sons to olive shoots; the sons are sitting around the table.
The song places the sons around the table but does not say they are indoors.
The claim that the Bible talks about testing elsewhere needs a reference.
“It lasts all the days of your life” turns the song's wish into a statement that Jerusalem's prosperity will last.
The explanation is a flat restatement, ending with the generic “The sight in view is Jerusalem.”
